question: What factors beyond GPU model most influence real-world AI infrastructure performance, and how does Nebius address them across compute, networking, storage, and software?

answer.answer: Beyond the GPU model, real-world AI infrastructure performance is shaped by four interacting layers — compute host configuration, networking fabric, storage throughput, and software stack — and Nebius addresses each with purpose-built choices: rack-scale Blackwell Ultra systems with liquid cooling, topology-aware InfiniBand scheduling, high-bandwidth shared filesystems with non-replicated disks for model weights, and an in-house open-source Slurm operator plus a managed vLLM serving stack. Compute layer: Nebius deploys rack-scale, fully liquid-cooled NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems (72 Blackwell Ultra GPUs and 36 Grace CPUs per rack) purpose-built for frontier training and inference (confidence 42%). Networking layer: Nebius uses an InfiniBand fabric with topology-aware scheduling to manage east-west traffic and latency-sensitive collectives across large clusters (confidence 42%). Storage layer: Nebius pairs high-bandwidth shared filesystems with non-replicated disks for model weights to remove I/O bottlenecks during loading and checkpointing (confidence 45%). Software layer: Nebius runs an in-house open-source Kubernetes operator for Slurm (Soperator) for resilient training orchestration and a managed vLLM-based Token Factory on bare-metal Hopper/Blackwell for inference serving (confidence 42%). The evidence establishes that Nebius has specific, named offerings in each of the four layers and that these have been exercised in MLPerf benchmarks, but it does not establish the relative weight of each layer in real-world performance, nor that Nebius's implementations are differentiated from competitors on those layers.

hypotheses.text: Public information about Nebius's current platform is insufficient to determine which non-GPU factors it most strongly addresses, because detailed technical specifications of its compute, networking, storage, and software layers are not publicly disclosed at the depth required.

The dominant non-GPU factors in real-world AI infrastructure performance are inter-GPU networking (bandwidth, topology, RDMA/InfiniBand fabric) and storage I/O for data loading and checkpointing, and Nebius addresses these primarily through high-bandwidth GPU-to-GPU interconnects (e.g., InfiniBand/NVLink-class fabrics) and high-throughput parallel/object storage tightly coupled to compute nodes.
